Rashi on Chullin 49a:10:1.english: A worm - A worm that emerges from the lung and perforated it.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:10:2.hebrew: קודם שחיטה פריש - מן הריאה ונקבה, ונטרפה:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:10:2.english: [It] emerged before slaughter - From the lung and perforated it, and [the animal] became a tereifa.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:12:1.english: Malokh the Arab - [He] who lived among the Arabs.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:12:2.hebrew: אין הלכה כרבי שמעון קאמר - לא אמר הלכה כרבי שמעון, אלא אין הלכה כרבי שמעון קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:12:2.english: He said: "The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon" - He did not say "the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon," but rather he said: "The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon."

Rashi on Chullin 49a:13:1.english: And you, what is in your hand - Rav Beivai asked Rabbi Zeira.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:14:1.english: And the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - The Gemara [itself] decides this. And in the final academy, these rulings that are decided anonymously in the Gemara were decided.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:15:1.hebrew: כהנים - שהקבה ניתנה להם מאת זובחי הזבח, נהגו בו היתר לאכלו. ומשום רבי ישמעאל נקיט ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:15:1.english: Priests - Since the abomasum is given to them from those who slaughter the sacrifice, they were accustomed to treat [its fat] as permitted, to eat it. And [Rabbi Oshaya] formulated it [specifically concerning priests] on account of Rabbi Yishmael.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:15:2.hebrew: וסימניך - שהוא התירה, ולא תשכח בשם מי נאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:15:2.english: And your mnemonic - That he permitted it, so that you will not forget in whose name it was stated.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:15:3.hebrew: ישמעאל כהנא מסייע כהני - תמיד הוא עוזרן ומיקל להם, ולקמיה מפרש היכא:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:15:3.english: Yishmael the priest helps the priests - He always assists them and rules leniently for them; and further on [the Gemara] explains where.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:16:1.english: What is this - Where does [Rabbi Yishmael] assist them?

Rashi on Chullin 49a:16:2.hebrew: ואני אברכם - רבי ישמעאל מוקי ליה אכהנים, ורבי עקיבא מוקי ליה אישראל:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:16:2.english: And I will bless them - Rabbi Yishmael applies it to the priests, and Rabbi Akiva applies it to Israel.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:19:1.english: And in what [way does he] help the priests - Since Rabbi Akiva also maintains [that there is] a blessing for the priests from another verse.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:19:2.hebrew: במקום ברכה לישראל - אצל ברכת ישראל, דהכי עדיפא, דמשמע שמתברכין הן עם השאר:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:19:2.english: In the place of the blessing for Israel - Alongside the blessing of Israel, for this is preferable, as it implies that they are blessed together with the rest.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:1.hebrew: עובי בית הכוסות - בסוף הכרס, שקורים פנצ"א, יש בו שעשוי ככובע, ושפת דופנו כפולה — שתי דפנות אדוקין זו בזו ושומן מחברן — וקורין לו דובלו"ן:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:1.english: The thickness of the reticulum - At the end of the rumen, which is called panse, there is [a part] shaped like a cap, and the edge of its wall is doubled — two walls clinging to each other, and fat connects them — and they call it doublon.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:2.hebrew: מצד אחד - שנקבה את דופן הפנימית, ולא נקבה את השנית:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:2.english: From one side - That it perforated the inner wall, and did not perforate the second [wall].

Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:3.english: [It is] kosher - For its fellow [wall] protects it.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:4.english: From both sides - That [the needle] perforated the second [wall] and emerged into the body cavity.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:5.hebrew: טרפה - ולא אמרינן, היכא דלא נקבה אלא את האחת: אי קופא לבר — שנמצאת קופא שלה תחובה בדופן, ופיה כולה בתוך הכרס — ודאי מבחוץ נכנסה, שנקבה את הוושט או כרס או דקין, ובאת לחלל הגוף, ומשם חזרה ונכנסה לעובי בית הכוסות, ועברה כבר כולה את הדופן החיצון, ולא הספיקה קופא שלה לעבור את דופן הפנימי (דאי מבפנים באתה, ועכשיו היא מתחלת לצאת דרך עובי בית הכוסות, אין דרך הקופא לנקב), ונימא טרפה? אלא מדקתני כשרה, שמעינן מינה: כל היכא דמצינו למימר סמפונא נקט ועל — כגון הכא, די"ל דרך הוושט באת עד הלום, ועכשיו היא מתחלת לנקב — ואפילו קופא לבר, לא טרפינן:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:1:5.english: [It is] a tereifa - And we do not say, in a case where it perforated only one [wall]: If the eye is facing outward — where its eye is found embedded in the wall and its point is entirely inside the rumen — it certainly entered from the outside, having perforated the gullet, or [the] rumen, or [the] intestines, and came into the body cavity, and from there turned back and entered into the thickness of the reticulum, and has already passed completely through the outer wall, while its eye has not yet managed to pass through the inner wall (for if it came from the inside and is now beginning to exit through the thickness of the reticulum, it is not the way of the eye to perforate), and let us say [that it is] a tereifa? Rather, from the fact that it teaches [that it is] kosher, we learn from it: Wherever we are able to say that it took a channel and entered — such as here, where it can be said that it came via the gullet until here and is now beginning to perforate — then even [if] the eye is facing outward, we do not deem [it] a tereifa.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:2:1.hebrew: אוכלין ומשקין דחקוה - ומתוך הדחק נכנסה קופא שלה בבשר. הילכך, אע"ג דקופא לבר, הואיל ולא חזינן נקב יוצא לחוץ — כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:2:1.english: Food and liquid pushed it - And due to the pressure, its eye entered into the flesh. Therefore, even though the eye [faces] outward, since we do not see a perforation exiting to the outside, [the animal is] kosher.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:3:1.hebrew: הונא מר טריף - דקסבר: נקובי נקיב, שלא נכנסה אלא דרך הוושט, ונקבה כרס או וושט או דקין, ויצתה:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:3:1.english: Huna Mar deemed [it] a tereifa - For he holds that it certainly caused a perforation, as it could only have entered via the esophagus, and it punctured the rumen, or the esophagus, or the intestines, and exited.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:3:2.hebrew: מכשר - כיון דבסמפונא אישתכח, אמרינן: מי מיכוונה להכנס בסמפון זה? אלא דרך הקנה נכנסה. והקנה וקנה כבד סמוכין זה לזה בהתחלקן סמוך לריאה, וגם קנה הלב וקנה הכבד מתחלקין לסמפונות בראשן האחד, וי"ל שנכנסה מסמפוני הכבד לסמפוני קנה הכבד, ומשם עלתה לכבד דרך הסמפונות:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:3:2.english: Deemed it kosher - Since it was found in the duct, we say: Could it have aimed to enter this duct? Rather, it entered via the windpipe. And the windpipe and the tube of the liver are adjacent to each other where they branch near the lung, and also the tube of the heart and the tube of the liver branch into ducts at their one end, and it can be said that it entered from the ducts of the liver into the ducts of the tube of the liver, and from there it ascended to the liver via the ducts.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:3:3.english: Take the robe of those who deemed it a tereifa - For they fed it to the dogs.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:2.hebrew: סימפונא - דכבד נקט ועל. דרך הקנה נכנסה, דאי דרך הוושט נכנסה — אינה ראויה לנקב כלום ולצאת משם, ולחזור וליכנס כאן דרך נקב:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:2.english: The duct - It took [the duct] of the liver and entered. It entered via the windpipe, for if it had entered via the esophagus, it is not capable of perforating anything and exiting from there, and then entering here through a perforation.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:3.hebrew: ואע"ג דלא נפקא - שאינה יכולה לצאת דרך הסמפון כשרוצין להוציאה, לפי שהסמפון דחוק:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:3.english: And even though it does not exit - That it cannot exit through the duct when one wishes to remove it, because the duct is narrow.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:4.hebrew: מירבל הוא דרביל - על ידי נענוע שנענעה הבהמה בהליכתה ימים רבים, נכנסה תמיד מעט מעט במקום דחוק שאינה יכולה עכשיו לצאת. מירבל — לשון כברה שמנענעים אותה, כמו אייתי ארבלא וקמרבל באלו מציאות (ב"מ כו:):
Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:4.english: It sifted through - Through the shaking that the animal shook in its walking over many days, [the pit] continually entered little by little into a confined place, [such] that it cannot exit now. *Mirbal* is an expression denoting a sieve, which one shakes, as in: “He brought a sieve and sifted” in [the chapter] *Elu Metzi’ot* (Bava Metzia 26b).

Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:5.hebrew: מיבזע בזע - במחט, ומאן דטריף במחט, טריף נמי בהא:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:4:5.english: It has pierced - [As in the case of] a needle; and whoever deems [an animal] a tereifa in [the case of] a needle, deems [it] a tereifa in this [case] as well.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:5:1.english: For eating - [For] those who eat it as it is.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:5:2.hebrew: או ע"י סמנין - כשמערבין סממנין המאירין את העינים, אף היא מסייעה עמם:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:5:2.english: Or through substances - When they mix [it with] medicinal substances that illuminate the eyes, it too assists alongside them.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:6:1.hebrew: אווזא בזוזא ריאה דידה בארבעה - כשהאווז נלקח בדינר, ריאה שלה שווה ד', לפי שהסממנין מעורבין בה:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:6:1.english: A goose for a dinar, its lung for four - When the goose is purchased for a dinar, its lung is worth four [dinars], because the medicaments are mixed into it.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:6:2.hebrew: ואי ס"ד - כמות שהיא מאירה, לינקוט אווז שלם עם הריאה בזוזא וליכול. ומאי דקאמר — הכי גרסינן: ואי ס"ד לאכילה, לינקוט בזוזא וליכול:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:6:2.english: And if it should enter your mind - [Meaning, that] as it is, it illuminates [the eyes], let him take an entire goose with the lung for a zuz and eat [it]. And as for that which it says — this is the text we read: “And if it should enter your mind [that it is] for eating, let him take [it] for a zuz and eat.”

Rashi on Chullin 49a:7:1.hebrew: היכא דממשמשא ידא דטבחא - אני שמעתי: במיצר החזה, שמתוך הדחק היד קורעת בצפרניו. וכמדומה אני: בכל מקום שהוא יודע שיכול לתלות — כגון נקב העשוי בסכין, או שתלשה מלמעלה בחזקה, ואח"כ נמצא שם נקב:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:7:1.english: Where the hand of the butcher handles - I heard [it explained as referring to] the narrow part of the chest, where due to the cramped space, the hand tears [the lung] with its fingernails. But it appears to me [that it applies to] any place where he knows that one can attribute [it], such as a perforation made by a knife, or where he tore it forcefully from above and afterward a perforation was found there.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:7:2.english: And the halakha is that we attribute [it].

Rashi on Chullin 49a:8:1.hebrew: מרישי כלי - מריש דרשנין, המשמיעין לעם את דבריו כשהיה דורש:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:8:1.english: [One] of the heads of the kalla - [One] of the chief expositors, who make his words heard to the people when he would expound.

Rashi on Chullin 49a:9:2.hebrew: דהא תלינן בזאב - דאמר בפ"ק (לעיל חולין ט.): בא זאב ונטל את בני מעיים, והחזירן כשהן נקובין — אין אומרים במקום נקב נקב:
Rashi on Chullin 49a:9:2.english: As we attribute [perforations] to a wolf - For it is said in the first chapter (above, Chullin 9a): [If] a wolf came and took the intestines and returned them when they were perforated, we do not say [that] it perforated [them] at the site of a [prior] perforation.

Tosafot on Chullin 49a:15:1.hebrew: כהנים נהגו בו היתר - ה"ה ישראלים; וכהנים דנקט — לפי שהקבה ניתנה לכהנים:
Tosafot on Chullin 49a:15:1.english: "The priests accustomed themselves to consider it permitted" - The same applies to Israelites; and [the reason] that it mentions priests is because the abomasum is given to the priests.

Tosafot on Chullin 49a:16:1.english: What is [this] "helps the priests" - For on account of [just] one instance, [the Gemara] would not have called him "helps the priests".

Tosafot on Chullin 49a:17:1.hebrew: והקדוש ברוך הוא מסכים על ידם - ולרבי ישמעאל לא איצטריך קרא להכי, דפשיטא דמסכים, כיון שצוה להם לברך:
Tosafot on Chullin 49a:17:1.english: "And the Holy One, Blessed be He, affirms their blessing" - And according to Rabbi Yishmael, a verse was not needed for this, as it is obvious that He affirms [their blessing], since He commanded them to bless.

Tosafot on Chullin 49a:18:1.hebrew: ואברכה מברכיך - ואפילו עובדי כוכבים המברכים את ישראל מתברכין, כדאיתא בירושלמי דברכות, דההוא עובד כוכבים דיהיב שלמא לרבי ישמעאל; אמר לו: "מלתך כבר אמורה". פירוש: איני צריך להחזיר לך שלום, שברכתך כתובה מ"ואברכה מברכיך":
Tosafot on Chullin 49a:18:1.english: “And I will bless them that bless you” - And even gentiles who bless Israel are blessed, as it is stated in the Yerushalmi in Berakhot that a certain gentile greeted Rabbi Yishmael; [Rabbi Yishmael] said to him: “Your word has already been spoken.” Explanation: I do not need to return a greeting to you, for your blessing is [already] written from “And I will bless them that bless you.”

Tosafot on Chullin 49a:20:1.hebrew: שאמר משום אבותיו מאי היא דתניא כו' - פירוש: קבלה היתה בידו של רבי אושעיא דרבי ישמעאל משום אבותיו התיר, אבל לא מתוך ברייתא זו דקדק. ולא גרסינן: "דברי רבי ישמעאל שאמר משום אבותיו", אלא "דברי רבי ישמעאל" סתם; דהא במסקנא מהפכינן ליה, ומפרש דמשום אבותיו דקאמר רבי אושעיא — היינו משום אבותיו, וליה לא ס"ל. והא דקאמר הכא: "שאמר משום אבותיו מאי היא" — היינו: אותה ברייתא שהתיר רבי ישמעאל חלב הקיבה, שאתה אומר שהוא משום אבותיו — מאי היא:
Tosafot on Chullin 49a:20:1.english: "That he said in the name of his forefathers — what is it? As it is taught, etc." - Explanation: Rabbi Oshaya had a received tradition that Rabbi Yishmael permitted [it] in the name of his forefathers, but he did not deduce [this] from this baraita. And we do not read: "The statement of Rabbi Yishmael, who said [it] in the name of his forefathers," but rather simply "The statement of Rabbi Yishmael"; for in the conclusion [of the Gemara] we reverse [the opinions], and [the Gemara] explains that "in the name of his forefathers" that Rabbi Oshaya said means [that he said it] in the name of his forefathers, but he himself does not hold [in accordance with it]. And that which [the Gemara] says here, "[Concerning that which] he said in the name of his forefathers, what is it?" — that is: That baraita in which Rabbi Yishmael permitted the fat of the abomasum, which you [Rabbi Oshaya] say was in the name of his forefathers — what is it?

Tosafot on Chullin 49a:4:1.hebrew: אבל דזיתא מבזע בזע - פירש הקונטרס: ולמאן דחייש במחט, חייש נמי הכא. ואם כן, הוה דלא כהלכתא, דקיימא לן הלכתא כרבי יוחנן דמכשיר לעיל. אבל נראה דאפילו רבי יוחנן — במחט הוא דתלינן שבאתה דרך הסמפונות; אבל קשייתא דזיתא, שהם גסים ואינן יכולין לבא בריווח דרך הסמפונות, חיישינן שמא ניקבה הוושט וחזר ונכנס בכבד:
Tosafot on Chullin 49a:4:1.english: "But [the pit] of an olive pierces" - Rashi explained: And according to the one who is concerned in [the case of] a needle, he is also concerned here. And if so, this would not be in accordance with the halakhah, as we maintain that the halakhah is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, who deems [the animal] kosher above. But it appears that even Rabbi Yoḥanan [would agree here]: It is [only] in [the case of] a needle that we attribute [its presence to the assumption] that it came through the ducts; but [as for] olive pits, which are thick and cannot pass easily through the ducts, we are concerned lest it perforated the esophagus and then entered the liver.
